Title: Error Page
Summary: Error page that displays request diagnostics and environment warnings.
Content:
## Error.razor **Path:** `Components/Pages/Error.razor` **Type:** Routable page component ### Route ```razor @page "/Error" ``` ### Content ```razor Error

Error.

An error occurred while processing your request.

@if (ShowRequestId) {

Request ID: @RequestId

}

Development Mode

Swapping to Development environment will display more detailed information about the error that occurred.

The Development environment shouldn't be enabled for deployed applications. It can result in displaying sensitive information from exceptions to end users. For local debugging, enable the Development environment by setting the ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT environment variable to Development and restarting the app.

``` ### State | Member | Type | Description | |--------|------|-------------| | `HttpContext` | `HttpContext?` | Cascading parameter from the hosting environment. | | `RequestId` | `string?` | The request identifier for diagnostics. | | `ShowRequestId` | `bool` | `true` if `RequestId` is not null or empty. | ### Lifecycle #### OnInitialized ```csharp protected override void OnInitialized() => RequestId = Activity.Current?.Id ?? HttpContext?.TraceIdentifier; ``` Resolves the request ID from `Activity.Current?.Id` (OpenTelemetry/W3C trace context) or falls back to `HttpContext.TraceIdentifier`. ### Routing Configured in `Program.cs` as the exception handler: ```csharp app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error", createScopeForErrors: true); ``` ### Notes - This page is **only shown in non-Development environments** for unhandled exceptions. - In Development, the Developer Exception Page is shown instead. - The `createScopeForErrors: true` parameter ensures a DI scope is created for error handling. - Does **not** display exception details to avoid information leakage in production.
